questions.question: A RAG application retrieves 10 documents, but only 2 are relevant to the user's question. Which improvement should be considered to improve the quality of the context passed to the LLM?

options.text: Remove the retriever and ask the LLM to answer directly
Increase the context window without changing retrieval
Introduce a reranking step to reorder retrieved documents by relevance

questions.explanation: A reranker evaluates retrieved candidates and reorders them based on their relevance to the query. This can improve the quality of the final context supplied to the LLM, even when the initial retriever returns noisy results.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of using delimiters around retrieved documents in a prompt?

options.text: To increase the number of tokens available to the model
To help distinguish trusted instructions from untrusted contextual data
To convert retrieved text into vector embeddings

questions.explanation: Delimiters make prompt structure clearer by separating instructions from contextual content. They help communicate trust boundaries but are not a complete defense against prompt injection. Additional validation and security controls are required.

questions.question: A team evaluates a RAG application using a test dataset containing questions and reference answers. Which evaluation approach measures whether the generated answer is factually supported by the retrieved context?
questions.explanation: Faithfulness evaluates whether the generated response is supported by the provided context. It is particularly useful in RAG systems for identifying unsupported claims and hallucinations.
